title: Making Open Models 10x faster and better for Modern Application Innovation: Dmytro (Dima) Dzhulgakov

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is Fireworks' custom serving stack built from CUDA kernels up, FireAttention technology, serverless inference, and latency/throughput optimization for production deployment of open models. Fireworks is a developer platform for serving and fine-tuning models that is used across general-purpose application verticals rather than a single industry. The talk covers production serving at scale—from serverless inference to enterprise contracts—serving over 150 billion tokens daily for production customers. Prerequisites include basic understanding of LLMs and inference serving, targeting intermediate-level practitioners familiar with open versus proprietary model tradeoffs. This is a recorded conference presentation delivered at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. All evidence anchors are sourced directly from the transcript with grade 'said_in_transcript'.

summary: Dmytro Dzhulgakov, co-founder and CTO of Fireworks AI and a PyTorch core maintainer for five years, presents Fireworks' approach to making open models production-ready. The founding team combines PyTorch leadership from Meta with Google AI veterans, bringing deep experience in productionizing AI at scale. He argues that while proprietary models like GPT-4 dominate current production inference, they impose high latency, high cost, and unnecessary generalization for narrow domains. Open models like Llama and Gemma, when fine-tuned, can match proprietary quality at up to 10x speed improvement, as benchmarked by Berkeley for function calling tasks. A cost example illustrates this: 10,000 users making 20 calls daily with 5K-token prompts on GPT-4 can cost approximately $10K/day or several million annually. Three key challenges with open models are identified: complicated setup and maintenance, optimization complexity, and production readiness. Fireworks addresses these with a ground-up custom serving stack spanning custom CUDA kernels to service-level orchestration, achieving top performance on Artificial Analysis benchmarks for long-prompt RAG. They are the fastest SDXL provider and the only SD3 serving provider. Their platform supports Gemma, Llama, ASR, TTS, and partner models. LoRA fine-tuning enables thousands of model variants on a single GPU with serverless per-token pricing. Dzhulgakov introduces compound AI systems as the emerging paradigm, where function-calling agents coordinate domain-specialized models, RAG, external tools, and APIs. Fireworks released FireFunction V, an open-source function-calling model available on Hugging Face, which combines free-form chat with multi-step function calling. A demo shows it querying stock prices, performing reasoning about cloud providers, and generating charts via external APIs, with contextual awareness for follow-up queries. The model supports structured generation with JSON grammar mode. Product offerings range from serverless per-token inference to on-demand dedicated hardware to enterprise-level contracts with personalized setup. Fireworks serves over 150 billion tokens daily for customers including Quora (Poe), Cursor, Sourcegraph, Upstage, and Linear. Per external LangChain state-of-stack data, Fireworks is the second most popular model-pulling platform after Hugging Face. The platform is OpenAI API-compatible and integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other frameworks.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.summary: Dzhulgakov introduces himself, noting co-founder Lino could not attend. He describes the founding team's background: PyTorch leads from Meta and Google AI veterans with a decade of production AI experience. Dzhulgakov personally has been a PyTorch core maintainer for five years, giving him deep commitment to open source. He believes open source models are the future for GenAI applications, which is Fireworks' focus.

sections.title: Open vs Proprietary Model Tradeoffs
sections.summary: Dzhulgakov contrasts proprietary models (one-size-fits-all, high latency, high cost, unnecessary generalization) with open models that excel in domain adaptability. Fine-tuned smaller models like Llama 3 can match GPT-4 quality at 10x speed for function calling. A cost example shows GPT-4 usage reaching ~$10K/day. Open models shine in customization with thousands of variants on Hugging Face for coding, medicine, language specialization, and more.

sections.title: Challenges of Open Models
sections.summary: Three challenges of open models are identified: (1) complicated setup and maintenance requiring GPU sourcing, framework selection, model downloads, and optimization tuning repeated with every model update; (2) optimization complexity with many use-case-dependent settings for latency, throughput, and prompt length; (3) production readiness requiring scalability, telemetry, observability, and dealing with unreliable public-cloud GPUs.

sections.title: Fireworks Solutions: Custom Serving Stack and Platform
sections.summary: Fireworks built a ground-up custom serving stack from CUDA kernels to service orchestration, tunable for custom latency/throughput/cost requirements. They achieve top performance on Artificial Analysis benchmarks for long-prompt RAG. They are the fastest SDXL provider and only SD3 provider. The platform supports Gemma, Llama, ASR, TTS, and partner models like E-large. LoRA fine-tuning enables thousands of model variants on a single GPU with serverless per-token pricing. Fine-tuning platform supports user datasets and live feedback collection.

sections.title: Compound AI Systems and Function Calling
sections.summary: Dzhulgakov introduces the concept of compound AI systems, where the model alone is not the product. Models hallucinate (requiring RAG), no universal multimodal AI exists yet (requiring model chaining), and external tools and actions are needed. Function calling serves as the core architecture, with agentic models coordinating domain-specialized models, external APIs, code interpreters, and tools. Fireworks focuses on function-specialized models, with details to follow in the next section.

sections.title: FireFunction V Demo and Open Source Model
sections.summary: Dzhulgakov demos FireFunction V, released two weeks prior, combining free-form chat with function calling. The demo app queries stock prices, performs multi-step reasoning (identifying top cloud providers as AWS, GCP, Azure), calls external APIs for stock quotes, and generates bar charts via a chart plotting API. Contextual awareness is demonstrated: adding Oracle to an existing graph maintains prior context, while switching topics drops irrelevant history. The demo is open source on GitHub, built with FireFunction and SDXL. The model itself is open source on Hugging Face and supports structured generation with JSON grammar mode.

sections.title: Product Offerings and Getting Started
sections.summary: Fireworks offers a tiered product range from early prototyping to enterprise scale. Serverless inference provides per-token pricing without hardware concerns. Users can fine-tune on-platform or bring their own LoRA adapters. On-demand dedicated hardware offers more customization for production-scale needs. Enterprise-level provides discounted long-term contracts with personalized hardware setup and performance tuning. The platform is OpenAI API-compatible, supporting existing clients and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex.

sections.title: Production Customers and Developer Adoption
sections.summary: Fireworks serves over 150 billion tokens daily for companies ranging from startups to enterprises. Customers include Quora (Poe chatbots), Cursor (code assistant where latency is critical), Sourcegraph, Upstage, and Linear. Per external LangChain state-of-stack data, Fireworks is the second most popular platform for model pulling after Hugging Face. Dzhulgakov invites developers to try the playground and visit their expo booth.
